name: Memcached
model: Flat cache of string keys to opaque byte values with expiry times; get, set, delete, increment, compare-and-swap
engine_note: Multithreaded in-memory hash table with slab allocator and LRU eviction; optional extstore spills cold values to flash
consistency: Single-key operations are atomic (with compare-and-swap); no multi-key transactions. No replication or persistence in the server: a restart or node loss loses its data, and full memory evicts old keys silently. Treat every value as disposable.
scaling: Add servers: clients hash each key to one server; servers do not talk to each other. More RAM or threads per box also works.
managed: Google Cloud Memorystore for Memcached (deprecated, shuts down 2029-01-31)
reach: Reach for it when you need a plain, very fast multithreaded cache of rendered results or query results and losing the cache is harmless.
avoid: Avoid when you need data types, persistence, replication, pub/sub or counters you must not lose; Redis or Valkey fit those better.
escape: Postgres cannot answer hot repeated reads at memory speed, and a cache miss is cheap to recompute.
chat: A cache of rendered chat lists or user profiles; the source of truth stays in Postgres.
notes: Google Memorystore for Memcached is deprecated: no new instances in new projects after 2027-02-01, shutdown 2029-01-31; Google points users to Memorystore for Valkey. The licence file is the original Danga Interactive BSD-style 3-clause licence. Memcached has a proxy mode (built-in router) that can do replication across pools; not covered here. No Jepsen report.
